input.rationale: Revise the fixed startup-replay experiment as a successor: keep the four retained cases and add one mechanism-isolating control that replays the identical 8193 committed entries with MaxAppendEntries=1024, so the same log state needs 9 batches instead of 129. This separates the batch count from the entry count and store state, and begins to close the unmeasured partial-replay limitation in the current interpretation.

scope.description: Five restart attempts with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: a commit-tracking store seeded with 8192 committed command entries (exactly 128 batches at MaxAppendEntries=64), the same seeded store with 8193 entries (129 batches), the same 8193 entries with MaxAppendEntries=1024 (9 batches), and two restarts of retained state produced by a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the normal leader/commit/apply path, one after an explicit Snapshot() and one without a snapshot.
assumptions: The FSM batch channel capacity (128) is a constant of the captured code; MaxAppendEntries is a validated configuration field and is recorded per case.
Each case builds its own stores and transport, so cases do not share state; the real-prefix cases reuse exactly the stores written by the producing raft.
NewRaft is invoked on its own goroutine and observed for a bounded window; a case that never returns is reported as returned=false rather than as a harness failure.
fsm_applied_sampled is a single observation at the end of the window, not a completion marker.
excluded: No assertions about commit safety, voting or membership; this probe addresses startup progress only.

Replay lengths produced by shortening a real-prefix snapshot partially (between 1 and 128 batches) are still not exercised; only the seeded 9-batch case and the 0-batch snapshot control bracket that region.

experiment.prefix: Per case the harness creates an InmemCommitTrackingStore (and InmemSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, assuranceFSM) and emits startup_case_<case> with the configured MaxAppendEntries, staged commit index, last log index, snapshot index and derived replay batch count. Seeded cases store LogCommand entries 1..N and stage commit index N; control_same_entries_larger_batches seeds the same 8193 entries as trigger_129_batches but builds its Config with MaxAppendEntries=1024. Real-prefix cases call BootstrapCluster for a single voter, start the producing raft with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, wait for leadership, apply 8300 commands through Apply futures on the leader, optionally call Snapshot(), then Shutdown(). The restart then calls NewRaft with a fresh Config (RestoreCommittedLogs=true), a fresh FSM and a fresh transport on the retained stores, bounded by the case timeout; startup_result_<case> records returned, elapsed_ms, error, sampled FSM apply count and the number of newly blocked processLogs/restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutines relative to a pre-case stack sample.
semantic_changes: The startup case event now records the MaxAppendEntries actually configured for that case rather than the default constant; the four retained cases still use 64.

New case control_same_entries_larger_batches admits an observation that can refute the mechanism: a return there, with the hanging case unchanged at 64, attributes the block to batch count rather than entry count.
experiment.responsibility: The library, not the caller, owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel: it chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh, and decides the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so it must complete for a legal (store, commit index) state rather than block the caller that cannot yet shut it down.

comparisons.description: Exactly 128 replay batches (the channel capacity) must still let NewRaft complete.
A real-prefix restart whose snapshot bounds the replay must let NewRaft complete.
The same 8193 committed entries replayed as 9 batches must let NewRaft complete; a failure here would attribute the block to entry count rather than batch count.
One entry past the 128-batch capacity must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
A real cluster restart with 130 replay batches must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.

experiment.revision_reason: Added case control_same_entries_larger_batches: identical 8193 committed entries and identical store state as trigger_129_batches, but Config.MaxAppendEntries=1024, which makes restoreFromCommittedLogs enqueue 9 batches instead of 129. Case events now record the actual max_append_entries used instead of the default constant.

result.summary: Submitted a successor experiment for the same question: the four retained cases plus a mechanism-isolating control that replays the identical 8193 committed entries with MaxAppendEntries=1024 (9 batches instead of 129). Native feedback showed that case returning NewRaft in 2 ms while the 64-entry-batch case still blocked, so the new receipt should attribute the stall to batch count rather than entry count; the interpretation still needs that receipt cited.
